title: Elvis Presley's D.J. Fontana (Modern Drummer interview, May 1985; republished 2018)
notes: Learned with a cousin in Shreveport, practised on pillows; listened only to big band and Dixieland; strip joints. The Hayride: behind a curtain the first week, then 'a snare drum, a stick, and a brush'; country singers want no fills. The Gretsch: 'a small tom, floor tom, bass drum, snare drum, a cymbal', a 22-inch bass drum, goatskin heads. Don't Be Cruel: Presley's leather guitar case, 'I popped it with one hand and used a stick in my other hand.' Jailhouse Rock: the lick for the rock-breaking scene, 'Scotty and I were piddling around and just lucked out on that lick.' 'Elvis wanted you to catch every leg movement.' 'I never was fancy.' In the studio 'they'd baffle all the drums and the guitars.'

title: Remembering D.J. Fontana, The Drummer For Elvis Presley's Band (Fresh Air, NPR; Terry Gross's 1987 interview, rebroadcast 20 June 2018)
notes: Gross on Hound Dog's roll: 'one of the most famous drum rolls in history. Did you have that one planned?' Fontana: 'We didn't ever plan anything'; it happened by accident and Presley had him keep it. 'When I was 15 years old, I was working strip acts down in Shreveport. So I learn to follow these people.' At the Cotton Bowl the band could not hear Presley: 'We only had three little pieces', and followed his hands, feet and legs. In the Jailhouse Rock film.

title: DJ Fontana, NAMM Oral History (interviewed 22 July 2001)
notes: Born 15 March 1931. Presley and Fontana at Herb Brochstein's drum shop in Houston, where Presley asked whether Brochstein's own kit was for sale. On Hound Dog, Jailhouse Rock, Treat Me Nice and All Shook Up; Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a sideman, 2009.

title: D.J. Fontana, Elvis Presley's Drummer, Dead at 87 (Jeff Tamarkin, Best Classic Bands, 13 June 2018)
notes: Born in Shreveport, 15 March 1931; drums from high school. The Hayride's house drummer; sat in with the trio on 16 October 1954, reportedly behind a curtain; a permanent member from November 1955; in the studio with Presley from 10 January 1956. 460 Presley recordings. Levon Helm (AP, 2004): 'it wasn't rock 'n' roll until D.J. put the backbeat into it.' Stan Lynch: 'There were no drum parts written for him on those Elvis records.' Later with McCartney, Ringo Starr, Jeff Beck, Johnny Cash, Dolly Parton, Keith Richards.

title: Elvis Presley's drummer set the beat that rock'n'roll continues to follow (The Post, Wellington, 21 June 2018)
notes: Read only through search-engine extracts: the page refused a direct fetch. Retells Peter Guralnick's Last Train to Memphis: Don't Be Cruel took 28 takes, and Fontana struck the back of Presley's leather-covered guitar, across his lap, with a mallet. His playing 'blended measures of restraint with explosive moments of energy'.

title: DJ's Gretsch Drums (scottymoore.net)
notes: A four-piece round-badge Gretsch in copper nitron ('Copper Mist'), an unshaven calfskin front head on the bass drum. Snare 5.5x14, tom 8x12, floor tom 14x14 (stolen, replaced with 16x16), bass drum 14x20; a 20-inch ride. Bought about 1954 from Herb Brochstein in Houston, his own set; not in photographs with Presley before September 1955. Photographs: The Milton Berle Show, 5 June 1956; Russwood Park, 4 July 1956; Buffalo, 1 April 1957; the Jailhouse Rock sessions at Radio Recorders, May 1957.

title: Elvis Presley (album) - Wikipedia
notes: Sessions at RCA Victor in Nashville on 10 and 11 January 1956 and in New York on 30 and 31 January. Blue Suede Shoes opens the album. Personnel: D. J. Fontana on drums but for I Love You Because, Just Because, Tryin' to Get to You, I'll Never Let You Go and Blue Moon (Sun recordings).
